AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: AGRICULTURE
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. About how high should a compost heap be built? (1 mark)
   A. As flat as the ground
   B. As high as a house
   C. About as high as your chest
   D. Only one hand high

2. Why does compost help the environment? (1 mark)
   A. It uses up all the water
   B. It kills all soil animals
   C. It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   D. It creates more rubbish

3. What is irrigation? (1 mark)
   A. Digging the soil
   B. Harvesting crops
   C. Spraying crops with medicine
   D. Giving water to crops by ways other than rain

4. Which animal is a domestic animal, not a wild one? (1 mark)
   A. Hare
   B. Goat
   C. Monkey
   D. Squirrel

5. Which animal often picks maize cobs and bananas? (1 mark)
   A. Monkey
   B. Cow
   C. Duck
   D. Hen

6. Why do we label the seedbed rows? (1 mark)
   A. To give plants names
   B. To remember the crop and the date sown
   C. To decorate
   D. To scare birds

7. What is a seedbed? (1 mark)
   A. A type of crop
   B. The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   C. A bed for sleeping
   D. A tool for digging

8. About how far apart may rows of tiny seeds be? (1 mark)
   A. 1 mm
   B. 15 to 20 cm
   C. 5 metres
   D. 10 metres

9. How far apart may passion fruit plants be planted? (1 mark)
   A. 10 cm
   B. Touching
   C. 30 metres
   D. About 2 to 3 metres

10. What is a grafted seedling? (1 mark)
   A. A seed in a bag
   B. A plant grown in water
   C. A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   D. A dead plant

11. Which of these is a benefit of growing your own fruit? (1 mark)
   A. Fewer vitamins
   B. Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   C. Less food
   D. More expenses

12. Why is mulch put around a young tree? (1 mark)
   A. It makes the tree shorter
   B. It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   C. It stops flowering
   D. It kills roots

13. What do leaves do for a fruit tree? (1 mark)
   A. Take in water from the soil
   B. Hold the tree in the ground
   C. Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   D. Make the trunk

14. What is the purpose of vaccinating animals? (1 mark)
   A. To make them heavier
   B. To colour them
   C. To make them noisy
   D. To prevent diseases

15. Which product does a dairy cow give? (1 mark)
   A. Eggs
   B. Feathers
   C. Milk
   D. Wool

16. What is meant by income from animals? (1 mark)
   A. Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   B. Manure used
   C. Feathers
   D. Food eaten at home

17. Which group of animals is called poultry? (1 mark)
   A. Zebras and giraffes
   B. Cows and bulls
   C. Sheep and goats
   D. Chickens, ducks and turkeys

18. Which domestic animal is often kept in dry areas for milk and meat? (1 mark)
   A. Rabbit
   B. Pig
   C. Duck
   D. Camel

19. Which of these gives fibre? (1 mark)
   A. Sweets
   B. Soft drinks
   C. Vegetables and fruits
   D. Sugar

20. What does proportion mean in a meal? (1 mark)
   A. The right amount of each kind of food
   B. The colour of the food
   C. The price of the food
   D. The number of plates

21. Why should we not skip breakfast? (1 mark)
   A. The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   B. Breakfast is a waste of money
   C. It makes you tired
   D. It is not real food

22. Which local vegetable is a protective food? (1 mark)
   A. Managu
   B. Rice
   C. Ugali
   D. Butter

23. What is the use of a hygiene log? (1 mark)
   A. Measuring rain
   B. Recording daily hygiene practices
   C. Counting money
   D. Listing games

24. Why should you wash hands after removing gloves? (1 mark)
   A. Hands may still have germs
   B. Gloves are wet
   C. Gloves are heavy
   D. To dry the gloves

25. Why should fingernails be kept short? (1 mark)
   A. Short nails grow faster
   B. Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   C. Long nails are heavy
   D. Nails are food

26. Why do we dust from high places to low places? (1 mark)
   A. Dust falls downward
   B. Low places are dirtier
   C. It looks better
   D. High places are easier

27. Which of these can be made into a mop? (1 mark)
   A. A shoe
   B. Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   C. A chair
   D. A basin

28. Where should clean PPE be stored? (1 mark)
   A. In a dry, clean place
   B. In a wet corner
   C. On the floor
   D. In a dirty box

29. How should you hold the cloth if you are right-handed? (1 mark)
   A. In the left hand while sewing with the right
   B. In your teeth
   C. Above your head
   D. Under your foot

30. How do you place pins for tacking? (1 mark)
   A. Across the line
   B. Only at the edge
   C. Not at all
   D. Along the line

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Why should vegetables not be boiled for a long time? (3 marks)

32. Describe how to make long and short tacking. (4 marks)

33. Describe how to boil eggs. (4 marks)

34. Give three uses of tacking stitches. (3 marks)

35. Plan a balanced supper using local foods and name the group of each food. (3 marks)

36. Give two ways in which drip irrigation saves water. (2 marks)

37. Explain how PPE should be stored and why. (4 marks)

38. Explain what a fruit is in plant growth. (2 marks)

39. Write a plan for growing a passion fruit plant from planting to harvest. (5 marks)

40. List three materials that can be used to make a scarecrow. (3 marks)

41. Explain how to sow tiny seeds in a drill. (4 marks)

42. Name three foods that are boiled. (3 marks)

43. Describe how to wash hands correctly. (4 marks)

44. Explain why it is best to choose fruits that suit your locality. (3 marks)

45. Give three ways of caring for a fruit crop. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
AGRICULTURE — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. C — About as high as your chest
   A heap that is too low loses heat and one that is too high is hard to turn.

2. C — It reuses wastes instead of throwing them away
   It turns waste into useful manure.

3. D — Giving water to crops by ways other than rain
   Irrigation means supplying water to crops artificially.

4. B — Goat
   Goats are kept by people.

5. A — Monkey
   Monkeys pick crops from farms near forests.

6. B — To remember the crop and the date sown
   Labels prevent confusion.

7. B — The piece of ground prepared for sowing seeds
   A seedbed is where seeds are sown.

8. B — 15 to 20 cm
   Rows are close but leave space for weeding.

9. D — About 2 to 3 metres
   Give climbers room.

10. C — A young tree joined with a branch from a good tree
   Grafted trees give good quality fruit sooner.

11. B — Fresh fruit for the family at low cost
   Growing at home saves money.

12. B — It keeps the soil moist and controls weeds
   Mulch reduces evaporation.

13. C — Use sunlight to make food for the plant
   Leaves make food using sunlight.

14. D — To prevent diseases
   Vaccination protects animals from diseases.

15. C — Milk
   Dairy cows are kept for milk.

16. A — Money earned from selling milk, eggs, meat or animals
   Farmers sell products to earn money.

17. D — Chickens, ducks and turkeys
   Poultry means birds kept for eggs and meat.

18. D — Camel
   Camels survive in dry regions.

19. C — Vegetables and fruits
   Fibre helps digestion.

20. A — The right amount of each kind of food
   Proportion means the right amounts.

21. A — The body needs energy and nutrients to start the day
   Breakfast gives energy for school.

22. A — Managu
   Managu is a green leafy vegetable.

23. B — Recording daily hygiene practices
   A log helps to form habits.

24. A — Hands may still have germs
   Germs can get on hands.

25. B — Germs and worm eggs hide under long nails
   Clean short nails prevent infection.

26. A — Dust falls downward
   Dust moves downward.

27. B — Strips of old cloth tied to a stick
   A cloth mop works well.

28. A — In a dry, clean place
   Damp PPE grows mould.

29. A — In the left hand while sewing with the right
   This is the usual way.

30. A — Across the line
   Pins across the line hold the layers.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Long boiling removes vitamins into the water, so they lose their goodness.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct point.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Mark a line; make a long stitch of about 2 cm on top; make a short stitch of about 0.5 cm underneath; repeat along the line; finish with a small back stitch.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

33. (4 marks)
   Answer: Put eggs in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil, boil gently for about 10 minutes, cool in cold water and peel.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four steps.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hold layers of cloth together, mark a line, keep hems in place, help to sew straight (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each use.

35. (3 marks)
   Answer: For example, rice (energy), fish (body-building), spinach (protective).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food correctly named and placed.

36. (2 marks)
   Answer: It gives water near the roots so little is wasted, and less water evaporates because only a small patch of soil is wet.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

37. (4 marks)
   Answer: Clean and dry, in a cupboard, rack or clean box, so it does not grow mould or spread germs, and labelled so it is used by the owner.
   Working / marking points: 2 marks for storing, 2 marks for reasons.

38. (2 marks)
   Answer: The part of a plant that holds the seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for part of a plant, 1 mark for holding seeds.

39. (5 marks)
   Answer: Build a trellis; dig and prepare a hole with compost; plant a seedling; water and mulch; tie the stem to the support; weed and prune; harvest ripe fruits and wash before eating.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct stage, up to 5.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Sticks or poles, old clothes, a sack, dry grass, string, tins, old CDs (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct material.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Make a shallow drill about 1 cm deep; mix seeds with sand; sprinkle thinly in the drill; cover lightly with fine soil; water gently.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

42. (3 marks)
   Answer: Potatoes, eggs, cassava, maize, beans, rice (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: Wet hands; use soap; rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs and nails for about 20 seconds; rinse; dry with a clean cloth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each of four correct steps.

44. (3 marks)
   Answer: They grow better in the local climate, give more fruit, and need less care and cost.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct reason.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watering, weeding, mulching, adding compost, pruning, protecting from animals (any three).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.
